sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
வெள்ளை நிற வேழமுகனே வேதமூலனே
வெள்ளை உள்ளமொடு அடியார்க்கருளிடுவாய்
sections.translit:
veLLai niRa vEzhamuganE vEdhamUlanE
veLLai uLLamodu adiyArkkaruLiduvAy
sections.en: Oh, elephant-faced Lord Ganesha, your complexion is frosty white. You are the source of all scriptures. Please bless all your devotees with your pure heart.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
கவிழ்ந்திடும் கமண்டல நீரில் நிறைந்தவனே
அவிழ்ந்திடும் அலைகடல் நுரையிடை அமர்ந்தவனே
sections.translit:
kavizhndhidum kamaNdala nIril niRaindhavanE
avizhndhidum alaikadal nuraiyidai amarndhavanE
sections.en: You existed in the water that dripped from the sage’s kettle after the kettle was toppled by a crow. You were seated on sea foam that formed from the agitation of the ocean’s waves.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
அடுத்து அடுத்து வரும் பிறவியெலாம் எனை
விடுத்து ஓடிடவும் வருகின்ற வல்வினைகளைத்
தடுத்துக் காத்திடவும் உன் மென்மலர்ப் பாதச் சீர்
எடுத்துப் பண்ணிசைத்து அன்பன் பாடலானேன்
sections.translit:
adutthu adutthu varum piRaviyelAm enai
vidutthu Odidavum varugindRa valvinaigaLaith
thadutthuk kAtthidavum un menmalarp pAdhach chIr
edutthup paNNisaitthu anban pAdalAnEn
sections.en: This devotee composed a prayer and started singing of the glory of your divine feet.  I know that your blessing will drive away the inevitable birth cycles and protect me from impending karmic events.

notes: The pallavi line 1, and anupallavi line 2, refer to the appearance of Lord Ganesha as Nurai Pillaiar / Swetha Vinayaka, rising from the churning of the milky ocean. The devas forgot to worship him prior to churning the ocean. Lord Indira realized the mistake and made an idol of Ganesha from the foam. After everyone at this event prayed to the idol, the nectar appeared. More details can be found in the links below: Tiruvalanchuzhi Temple Sthalapuranam Kabartheeswarar Temple Legend Another anupallavi line refers to the origin story of the sacred Kaveri river. Lord Siva sent Vinayaka to generate water for the drought stricken South. Sage Agastya was also heading in the same direction. He always carried a sacred pot or Kamandalam. He decided to worship Lord Shiva at his usual prayer time and left the kamandalam in the custody of a little boy. When he returned, the little boy - who was none other than Ganesha - was gone and a crow was sitting on top of the pot. The crow, too, was Ganesha in disguise. The crow ran away, frightened by the sage, and toppled the pot. The water flowed without bounds and became the river Kaveri. For details see: Ganesha and Kaveri River Ganesha, Agasthiar and Cauvery/Ponni Origin of Melacauvery
